entries.definition: Appears to be a character in the game being played on stream; chat talks about visiting her and jokes about her personality alongside the emote coMMMMfy.
The country; chat is asking for or reacting to Bulgaria travel videos on stream.
Hard laughter at something absurd, embarrassing or ironic.
Marks a moment as great to watch: drama, a dramatic result, a collapse or a reveal.
Exasperation: posted at someone who said or did something dumb or annoying.
Agreement: posted after quoting or naming someone to say they are right, sometimes sarcastically next to COPIUM.
"Simple as": posted after a blunt answer to say there's nothing more to it.
A strong-man face posted to approve of a bold or winning move; in these chats it sits next to wins, threats to opponents and RapThis spam.
A cheerful cat for liking something or calling it a W; often spammed in a row.
Suspicion: a side glance at something weird or at someone acting off.
An alert bell for getting attention: chat puts it around breaking news, results to check and calls to look at something now.
Gloating at someone who just lost an argument or got dunked on; often paired with insults, SNARKED and SpeedLaugh.
Confused and lost: posted with "idgi" or when chat can't follow what's happening.
A siren for urgent news: in these chats it flags new results, projections, needle moves and Polymarket swings.
Cozy contentment: feeling comfy or pleased.
Celebration: posted on good news for chat's side, such as an opponent losing or getting snarked.
Disbelief or disgust at something said or shown.
A dancing emote for vibing, usually spammed in a row.
Excitement or hype, also used for greetings and goodbyes.
Goofy shrugging: used with "idk", odd questions and offhand jokes.
Nodding along: agreement with a claim or prediction, sometimes ironic.
Taunting laughter at a loser, spammed in long rows; in these chats paired with insults at opponents.
Waiting for an answer: posted after a question to chat or the stream.
Hype for a win or a dunk, usually spammed with GIGACHAD.
Sad and annoyed at once; posted with complaints.
Teasing accusation: "I know what you are", posted at suggestive or suspicious lines.
Excited pointing at something on screen.
Bowing in respect to someone or something impressive, often spammed.
A DGG heart: affection, congrats, greetings and birthday wishes.
Cope: refusing to accept bad news ("ITS NOT OVER COPIUM"), aimed at oneself or at others.
Surprise or disbelief at something said or shown.
Paranoid or unhinged talk, posted with conspiratorial or rambling lines.
Used to call on chat moderators to deal with a user, and in talk about the moderators of subreddits chat was looking at.
A dancing celebration emote, spammed in rows; in these chats also around "vote" calls.
Mock approval or resignation, tacked onto odd personal admissions and complaints.
A slow turtle: for slow loading or slow takes, sometimes spammed as a wall.
"Come on England": a mock-British cheer, used for urging something on.
Shock or outrage at something unforgivable or ridiculous, often spammed.
Victory: in these chats the main emote for Democratic wins on election night 2026 ("BLUE WAVE").
Posted when someone is caught out saying or doing something, as a tease.
The Grand Theft Auto games, mostly GTA 6; chat discusses its release and whether people on stream will play it.
A wave hello or goodbye.
Fights between streamers and community members; in Nov 2026 it meant an orbiter dispute over a meet-up, which chat followed for hours on stream.
A stream that a chatter has embedded on destiny.gg for others to watch; "top embed" is the most watched one and "ban the embed" asks for a stream to be pulled.
Plotting: posted with schemes, tactics and someone being invited into a call.
A running joke in chat about someone's Pepsi habit, usually alongside other junk-food jokes.
Pointing up at what's on stream or what was just said, often with "holy".
Mocking or hate-watching someone; chat used it for streamers and chatters going after each other in the Nov 2026 drama.
Mockery aimed at a person or community, as in "snark him"; also the drama content itself ("such good snark").
"Let him cook": let someone finish their idea, often ironic when the idea is bad.
An emote posted on its own when chat feels empty or quiet, for example after the stream ends.
Mostly part of diet pepsi or diet coke, a running joke about someone on stream wanting diet soda and lasagna.
Mocking goodbye to someone who lost or got banned.
The video game GTA 6; chat is talking about its release, preloading it and playing it, often with hype emotes.
Mild shock or a deadpan reaction.
Forced calm while things go badly ("WE HAVENT CALLED IT YET ItsFine"); often paired with COPIUM.
Appears to be the name of a streamer or show that chat mentions watching; the lines don't make it clear what it is.
Ordinary agreement, often as 'fair nuff'; also spammed in short 'seems fair' replies during the stream.
A running joke on stream about someone wanting or being denied diet pepsi, often paired with lasagna.
Spiked sharply during the stream's debate about whether there is a white or American culture. Chat uses it in arguments and in jokes about what counts as culture.
Emote and word posted in reply to a message chat sees as deliberately provocative, often with Clap.
"One guy": calling out that one person is behind something, or pointing at the one person who did it.
A streamer whose GTA game stream chat is following and linking; chat reacts to his progress and play.
Refers to the H3H3 channel and podcast; chat is following an ongoing drama around it that the stream covered.
During a stream segment on population genetics, dogs and dog breeds were the main analogy chat argued over, alongside wolves and selective breeding.
Chat discussed a news story about Nvidia chips reaching China and its politics.
Used several ways: AI training data in an AI research discussion, the Star Trek character Data during a TNG watch, and the 'overloaded with data' outage explanation.
An emote spammed in bursts, usually on its own, sometimes alongside the word shoot.
A person who follows a streamer mainly to mock them; chat throws the label at critics and at people it suspects of hate-watching.
Streams that chatters embed for others to watch in DGG chat; chat jokes about the embed rankings and about snarking at the embeds.
An emote chat spammed on its own; the lines don't show a clearer meaning beyond a link to an "orb".
A phone-call greeting ("hello"), used to get someone's attention or as a joke opener.
Appears to be a streamer chat talks about. Mentions include a video, TwitchCon, and arguments over bans in chat.
Partly ordinary soda; partly a nickname for the streamer Sodapoppin, discussed alongside another streamer over a game exploit and whether they would be banned.
The PlayStation 5; chat is talking about preloading and playing GTA 6 on it and comparing it with Xbox.
Mostly appears in "cop slop", chat's label for cop-genre movies or shows, used with CINEMA and GODSTINY.
Used in talk about race realism and race science during the genetics segment; chat mostly mocks those arguments.
Plural of snarker: people who watch or follow someone mainly to mock them.
Text-to-speech donation messages read out on stream; chat comments on TTS being on, paused or left running.
Spiked with a news story about Nvidia chips and China that chat discussed, plus unrelated mentions.
"It's over": despair at bad news, a bad needle move or infighting.
A fish emote chat spams, often on its own or alongside Clap and other emotes; it rose during fishing-related talk.
Tongue-in-cheek title chat uses for a particular community figure, often with mock respect emotes like IKneel and SoyPoint.
Appears to be a main playable character in the GTA game streamers are playing; chat comments on her character and asks streamers to switch to playing as her.
Refers to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whom chat discussed alongside a news story about Nvidia and China.
Appears to be a name chat treats as a running joke around the streamer awards' rising-streamer category; chat cheered for it, asked where it was, and complained it wasn't nominated or didn't win.
Attention and status; "clout chaser" is the insult chat throws at people it thinks join drama for views.
An AI model chat joked about, for example asking it to fix problems or blaming it in jokes about the flight stoppage.
Mostly in 'research stream', chat's name for long streams spent reading studies, here on genetics and race.
An emote posted on its own or after someone's name, appears to be used as a peeking or lurking reaction.
Used mainly in the joke about a local burger joint giving equity to a part-time high school student, from the work-and-pay debate.
An emote chat spammed on its own or in long repeated rows; the lines don't show a clearer meaning.
The chip company, which chat talked about as a stock pick, for its GPUs, and in news stories about its chips.
Mostly refers to commentator Tim Pool; sometimes other people named Tim.
A streamer or creator in Destiny's social circle who appears on or around his streams.
Short videos the stream was scrolling through; chat reacts to and comments on them.
Ordinary word for technology, used in mixed ways such as tech bros, game tech trees and film tech.
Appears to be a streamer chat often mentions alongside Destiny; this week chat mostly joked about him streaming as a penguin avatar.
Part of a running joke on stream about someone wanting lasagna and diet pepsi.
A general word that spiked across unrelated conversations about theft and taking credit.
Streamers and creators in Destiny's social circle; chat compares them and argues about how they treat DGG.
Everyday word. Chat talks about meals and tells the streamer their dinner is ready so they should go live.
Mostly AI models, in a chat discussion about training, reasoning and hardware needs.
An emote chat posts to react to something going badly while acting calm.
Mostly Stephen Miller, discussed as a Trump administration figure, with some lines about the musician Mac Miller.
Used for several different people named David; most lines appear to address a David appearing on stream, and others mention names like Pakman and Bowie.
Slang suffix meaning 'that kind of thing', added after a word or emote to describe a vibe.
Used for brown eyes in eye-color genetics talk, and appears in political names chat mentioned alongside election results.
Mostly snack chips during movie time, plus some talk of chip exports and GPU sales.
Refers to the shared movie-night "theater"; chat jokes about the empty theater, fires in the theater and the new theater intro.
Chat's name for low-stakes internet drama content, used both to complain about it and to cheer for more.
A general word used in several discussions, including gaming companies and tech and AI investment.
Part of a repeated spam line with the FISHIES emote about visiting Ireland.
Mostly about dirt blocks and dirt towers being built on stream in a block-building game.
Used in chat jokes about buying stocks (especially Nvidia) and about the stock market during an outage.
Mostly refers to the Kerch/Crimean bridge that chat says was hit and burning; also used in the sense of burned bridges between online figures.
Mostly refers to Ezra Klein and his Hasan interview, with some jokes about Ethan Klein.
Posted with the Dancer emote while the stream or a video is loading or about to start, as a group cheer.
The Palestinian militant group, which chat brought up in its Israel-Palestine arguments and in reaction to Hasan's views.
Mostly used as part of "Riemann Hypothesis", as chat reacts to claims that an AI solved or helped solve it.
Used in theater-style jokes during movie viewings, with chat pretending to eat, share or spill popcorn.
Ordinary word; the spike mostly comes from chat discussing a short meeting between Trump and other world leaders.

A math problem chat is suddenly talking about, appearing to react to claims that an AI (Claude) solved or helped solve the Riemann Hypothesis. Posted with surprise, jokes and requests for the stream to cover it.
An everyday word spiking alongside Dancer emote spam, with chat calling for dancing or telling others to stop dancing.
Ordinary word; spiked mainly through the repeated joke about a local burger joint giving equity to a part-time student.
The horror genre; chat discusses horror movies and survival horror games while watching a movie on stream.
An in-person event; in these chats mostly the election-night meetup around Destiny's stream and other streamer events chat compared it to.
Mostly chat spamming that Destiny should check his Discord DMs, often with ALARMA.
Chat asking the streamer and others to play the new GTA game, or noting who is playing it.
An emote chat spammed during the streamer awards, often alongside jokes about Hasan not winning an award.
The new Grand Theft Auto game that streamers, including ones chat follows, have started playing.
Used for a boat collision news story chat was reacting to, with ALARMA and jokes.
Short for developer; comes up in chat's talk about coding jobs, game dev, AI coding tools and getting a developer on stream to debate.
Chat is discussing reports that Poland was hit by rockets, with talk of Russia, NATO and invoking Article 4 or 5.
Chat discussing the new GTA game being console-only for now, buying a console for it, and teasing console players.
The AI company. Chat is posting about buying it or about its share price falling.
Frames per second; chat is arguing about the new GTA game's frame rate on consoles and how noticeable 30 versus 60 is.
Ordinary word with no special meaning in these lines, used in many unrelated ways.
Mostly about an Apple outage chat was noticing, with services like iCloud and Apple Pay reported down.
Mostly the '50 billion' funding request chat ties to the air traffic outage, repeated as a joke that people owe or need 50 billion.
Ordinary word with mixed uses: a song chat jokes about, and asking the streamer to boot up a game or stream.
Used in jokes about Hasan's suits during his Ezra Klein interview, especially calling it a Mao suit.
The AI company; chat discusses it next to Anthropic and Google, its models, its work on math problems, and AI lobbying and competition.
An emote posted on its own or alongside RapThis as a hype or approval reaction.
A common first name used for several different people. Chat doesn't use it as one shared reference.
Refers to Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer; chat is arguing over whether he and Hakeem Jeffries should keep their leadership roles.
Chat noting which streamers are playing the new GTA game, and asking why others are not.
Chat reacting to the streamer drinking wine on stream, with jokes about "wine mom" energy.
Mostly in 'data centers'; chat discusses building data centers, their jobs, water and power use, and local approval.
Used for the streamer awards show and its categories (such as hidden gem and rising streamer), including who won and who didn't.
Used in jokes about rewriting software from scratch, especially rewriting things in Rust or having AI rewrite them.
Elon Musk, whom chat is discussing in connection with his companies, Starlink and politics.
Refers to House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, discussed alongside Schumer in chat's argument over Democratic leadership and the speaker race.
Used in general chat about the U.S. military, including budgets, bases and Hegseth, and jokes about working your way up from Wendy's to the military.
Comes from a lobster-trapping scene in the GTA game; chat jokes about lobster size limits, lobster gauges and lobster cops.
General word with no single meaning; used in jokes about hiding things and guesses about what someone is hiding.
A word chat repeats as a joke about Hasan's vocabulary, usually with DANKMEMES and words like "actively deploying".
The Texas races on election night 2026, mostly the Senate race; chat asked for updates, called it early and joked that Texas was blue ("blexas").
An everyday word as chat talks about watching documentaries, including wanting one about the making of GTA 6.
Coping with a loss; on election night 2026, "cope cam" meant putting the other side's reactions (for example Fox News) on stream.
Microsoft's game console; chat compares it with the PS5 and discusses playing GTA 6 on it.
Ordinary word, mostly in an AI alignment and AI research discussion, plus movie talk.
Chat is reacting to a stock market drop, often posting that it is "cooked" and joking about who or what caused it.
Refers to Sean Duffy, who the lines show giving a press conference about an aviation communication breakdown and asking for funding; chat mocks the funding request and argues about his record.
Refers to the lobbying group AIPAC; chat mostly invokes it ironically or as a punchline when discussing who funds Democratic politicians.
Mostly about planes being grounded during the air traffic system breakdown chat is following, plus jokes about funding and AI flying planes.
Chat's link tag to xqc's stream on Kick, posted to point others at what is happening on his GTA stream.
Mostly about a lobster-trapping scene in the GTA game; chat jokes with mock outrage about undersized or 'baby' lobsters being caught.
Chat discussing Mormons and their beliefs and practices, mostly as trivia, jokes and questions.
Used while watching a video game movie adaptation on stream; chat debates whether video game movies can be good.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it for whether animals or groups can interbreed, often with the dogs-and-wolves example.
The stock ticker for Nvidia. Chat is posting about its price falling and about buying shares.
Used in chat's commentary on the outfits at the streamer awards, including a best-dress category.
General word appearing in 'bare minimum' and in a minimum wage policy discussion, plus 'should be 60fps minimum' about the GTA game.
Chat debating AI data centers: their energy and cooling, jobs, and politics around them.
Posted mockingly, often in caps, to tease someone who calls themself an empath; chat treats the label as a joke.
James Talarico, the Democrat in the 2026 Texas Senate race against Paxton; chat followed his lead all election night.
Chat's name for cop movies or shows; chat asks for more of them to be watched on stream.
Chat is using it mostly about Nvidia's leadership, joking about who the company's next CEO will be.
Mostly about wanted-level stars in the game being played on stream, plus a few unrelated uses.
Computer memory; chat complains about RAM prices and jokes that Sam Altman and AI data centers are taking all of it.
Mostly in 'real homies hour', said during a late or quieter part of stream when only the regulars are around.
Chat discussing fishing and fishing laws (licenses, lobster and size limits) during a stream segment on the topic, plus some figurative uses.
A conservative political commentator chat is joking about and arguing over, including talk of a movie of his being watched in the community.
Mostly computer memory: chat discussing memory bandwidth, unified memory and RAM production for running AI models and GPUs.
Spiking in talk about cyber attacks and national security, and in a running joke about a "Cyber 9/11".
Chat's word for animated avatar streaming, mostly asking Destiny to bring back a vtuber model and joking about Hutch's penguin avatar.
Refers to the movie The Odyssey, which chat says was shown during a movie night; chat is reviewing it and asking about rewatching it.
The movie theater, used while chat watches a movie together and recalls seeing it in theaters.
A Democratic politician chat argues about, with some asking for a stream mocking him.
The studio behind the GTA game chat is watching streamers play; chat praises or criticizes its games, console-only release and 30fps cap.
An everyday word, mostly in cute or joking posts about a tummy hurting or being full.
Comes up in general talk about politics, AI content, bots spreading narratives and regulating social media.
In the Nov 2026 orbiter drama, chat argued over who made or didn't make plans to meet up, and whose fault it was.
Refers to Pete Hegseth; chat criticizes him and discusses an impeachment vote involving him.
Posted with the CINEMA emote as mock or real applause for something that just happened on stream.
Refers to the penguin avatar Hutch appears to be using on stream; chat joked that Hutch is a penguin and asked where Destiny's own penguin avatar was.
Mostly refers to streamer Kai Cenat, whom chat cheered or mocked during the streamer awards.
Chat is using it about the beauty and makeup-community drama being watched on stream, often asking to move on from it.
Used in debates about wages and the minimum wage, apparently prompted by the Jubilee video about work and pay.
A general word used in several senses, including security guard in a story chat was discussing and the old guard of a political party.
Came up during the stream's debate about culture and race. Chat uses it while arguing over what counts as American culture and naming examples, many of them jokes.
Refers to a person named Mehdi whose interview or debate footage chat is watching; chat argues about his stance on Israel and Palestine and compares him with Whick as a debater.
A common first name used for several different people. The most frequent is someone chat discusses doing a stunt on stream.
Chat asking when the streamer will attempt or has beaten an "ender" boss fight in a game, apparently scheduled for a set time.
Mostly part of the name Van Hollen, a politician chat is discussing. It also shows up in jokes about someone living in a van.
Chat is commenting on someone's mustache, arguing over whether it looks good.
JD Vance, who chat refers to as standing near Trump during a televised event, with chat reacting to his facial expressions and speculating about future presidential runs.
Mostly appears as part of the fried rice chant from the culture debate. It also shows up in the slang sense of someone being burned out.
Appears to be a streamer chat mentioned during the streamer awards, asking whether he was there.
Appears to be a streamer whose stream or video Destiny was watching, with chat calling for him with DinkDonk and ALARMA.
The South Carolina Senate race, which chat flagged on election night 2026 when odds and early results looked close.
Appears to be a boss enemy in Minecraft that someone on stream is preparing to fight, with chat giving tips and joking about a past attempt.
A political label chat repeats, mostly mockingly, about someone who appears to have called himself or worn a hat saying "dark MAGA"; chat contrasts it with plain MAGA.
Mixed uses: a chatter going to a lake to stream fishing, and jokes about lobsters supposedly being in a lake, often with CORNPOP.
Mostly from "Grand Theft Auto", the video game chat is talking about playing.
Requests for a short summary of drama for people who just tuned in.
An emote chat spammed in reaction to something on stream, sometimes alongside the phrase "2nd puberty".
Ordinary word with mixed uses in chat, such as asking whether someone will address a claim or point.
A general word that spiked across several discussions, including ethnic and immigrant groups in the culture debate and interest groups in political talk.
Used sarcastically about safeguards that chat says are failing, both for AI and for political institutions.
Appears to be a daily puzzle game. Chat posts emoji result grids and asks whether others have played it.
A recurring meme posted with the FeelsOrbMan emote, as in pointing at or showing off 'the orb'; some chatters say they don't get it.
Plural of culture. It spiked during the stream's debate about white and American culture and the subcultures inside it.
Mostly refers to Sarah Longwell of the Bulwark, often alongside JVL; chat suggests Destiny do a stream or collab with her.
Short for Red Dead Redemption 2, which chat uses as the comparison point for the new GTA game's graphics, assets and performance.
Refers to Jubilee, a debate-video channel; the stream watched a Jubilee episode featuring Kevin O'Leary and chat largely dismisses the format as shallow 'slop'.
Comes up in chat's argument over whether software developers deserve the title of engineers or are just code monkeys.
Refers to a political commentator chat often criticizes; chat discusses his tweets, retweets and a recent video about a Hegseth impeachment vote, and mentions a planned event with Destiny.
Used in chat's verdicts on how the newly released GTA game looks, ranging from 'so good' to 'mid', often comparing it to RDR2.
Refers to Mark Carney, as chat names him in Canada-related discussion; chat is debating his trade dealings, including with China.
Running joke about undersized lobsters caught in a lobster-trapping scene in the GTA game, treated with mock outrage and 'find the baby lobsters' calls.
A repeated line telling someone to do this in real life, followed by the Dancer emote; it appears to be copied spam during dancing moments.
Ordinary phrase; used in the burger-joint equity joke and in discussion of education and whether finishing high school should be required.
Same as '30 fps': chat's reaction to the new GTA game being capped at 30 frames per second on consoles, including the PS5 Pro.
The IMAX (often 70mm) format chat says they saw the Odyssey movie in, used when rating it and comparing the theater experience.
A panel discussion people in chat watched or took part in; chat reviews how it went and who did well.
Part of the Nov 2026 drama among Destiny's orbiters: chat argued over who was or was not invited to hang out during his election trip.
Spam built around the Dancer emote, with chat telling each other to dance, often in long chains alternating the emote with words.
The sleep supplement; chat is swapping experiences and opinions about taking it, including long-term use.
Mostly puns on Crimea ('Crimea river', 'cry me a river bridge') during discussion of the bridge strike, plus unrelated uses.
Used for the streamer awards show, mostly in the phrase "streamer awards" and in jokes about who cared about winning.
Appears to be initials for a commentator chat is discussing, mostly his looks and his takes on Democrats and leftists.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat argues over what defines a species, using dogs and wolves as the main comparison.
Slang chat uses for praising someone excessively or uncritically, e.g. hyping a person or a game.
James Bond; chat is reacting to what the lines describe as news of the next Bond actor, mostly Robert Pattinson.
Chat talking about Dancer, which appears to be a newly added (possibly limited-time) dancing emote; people react to it and spam it between words.
Used in political discussion about populism. Chat argues over whether populist messaging and policy are good for Democrats.
Usually refers to actor Patrick Stewart, whose movies chat says it polled for movie night; sometimes other people named Stewart.
Posted with laughing emotes to mock someone's "real voice" being heard, apparently someone on stream or in a clip.
The 2026 Alaska races, mainly Peltola's; chat waited for the slow count to see if the Senate could reach 56.
Saturday Night Live; chat is reacting to SNL skits shown on stream and asking for more or fewer of them.
Dog breeds, which chat compared using FST during the genetics segment.
Mostly refers to Kevin O'Leary in the Jubilee video the stream watched; chat debates and mocks his arguments about work and getting rich.
Chat pleading with the streamer to play a clip, call or audio being discussed.
Posted while the stream appears to be playing Minecraft, with chat giving tips about turning raw copper into blocks; also joked about with data centers and wires.
Appears to be a streamer chat backed during the streamer awards, often with IKneel, and called robbed when she didn't win.
Mostly about software engineers, used as a counterexample in the work-and-pay debate and in jokes about a participant's job.
Used for a big target chat wants to take down, the "white whale", and for big-spending donors ("whale money").
Almost always 'allele frequency' in the population-genetics segment.
Mostly from "Grand Theft Auto", the video game, as chat talks about playing GTA 6.
Spiked during the culture debate. Chat uses it to discuss white and American identity and how identity differs from culture.
Used in the dog-versus-wolf analogy chat argued about during the genetics segment, plus some jokey self-descriptions.
Refers to a documentary or segment on the history of concrete that chat watched or voted on in a poll. Chat jokes about how boring or interesting it was.
Used to describe a long, wandering speech chat is watching, mostly by Trump.
Mostly refers to a video segment chat calls 'the academy' during a long reviewed video, plus mentions of Khan Academy; posted with CINEMA.
An emote chat posts on its own or in spam bursts with other emotes; chat calls the spam rare.
A common misspelling of Mehdi, used the same way while chat watches and argues about his older and newer interview footage.
Chat's name for long streams spent reading and reacting to research, here on genetics.
Used in chat debates over whether and how much the minimum wage should rise, apparently prompted by the Jubilee video on work and pay.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat compares wolves and dogs to argue about breeding and species boundaries.
Mostly Robert Pattinson, whom chat is discussing as the next James Bond, per the lines.
Refers to the debate prompts in the Jubilee video; chat mocks participants, including Kevin O'Leary, for misreading or not answering the prompt.
Mostly from "vocal fry", which chat is complaining about in someone's voice on stream. It also turns up in copy-pasted spam.
Part of Van Hollen, a politician chat is discussing. The talk centers on whether he or Schumer should get party support and on an interview with him.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it for which genes a study selected and what graphs of them show.
Chat's complaint that the new GTA game runs locked at 30 frames per second on consoles; some say it is unplayable, others say it is fine.
The grocery store chain; chat was talking about it while watching a video about Aldi on stream and comparing it to other grocers.
Running joke where chat insists things (tickets, cars, a gun) were "thrifted", appears to be mocking someone's claim about how they got something.
Refers to Marco Rubio, as chat names him; chat argues over his statements on Ukraine's satellite access and about his ethnicity.
Chat discussing the Mormon faith, including questions about a church-run college and whether people in the news were Mormon.
A Democratic politician chat is discussing as a possible replacement for Schumer, including talk of an ad and his record.
Name of a politician chat discusses as a possible Democratic Senate leader in place of Schumer, often posted with hype emotes.
The Browns NFL football team; chat reacts to a Browns game against the Saints.
The Dancer emote posted with "yuh" as a short dance or hype spam.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it alongside differentiation, variation and FST while arguing about group differences.
Appears to be an online personality chat expects to have a conversation or debate with others such as NSE, Erudite and Kyla; chat asks when it will happen.
The prediction market chat checked for live odds on election night 2026, especially swings in the Mississippi race.
Used while chat discusses reports of a strike on the bridge to Crimea and what it means for Russia and Ukraine; chat jokes about a 'Crimea beach party' and 'Crimea river'.
Ordinary word used as a reaction ("it's stale") and spammed with emotes; also some technical uses.
Mostly refers to the movie Heat, which chat watched on stream; chat asks about a sequel and complains about missing it.
Used in an AI discussion about what hardware models need, and in blaming the air traffic outage on hardware that could not handle new software.
Refers to the Kerch bridge; chat is reacting to reports that Ukraine struck it and it was on fire, often with RIPBOZO or CINEMA.
A running joke about a firepit (and a firepit meetup), usually posted with SCHIZO and laughing emotes, with chat suggesting the firepit never existed.
Refers to Chris Hansen, the TV host chat links to the movie Primetime; chat is asking for his take on the film and passing around his reported comments about it.
Refers to journalist Ezra Klein, whose interview with Hasan chat watched and argued about, mostly over how much he pushed back.
"Catching strays": getting criticized in passing when an argument was aimed at someone else.
Chat discussing getting the new GTA game to 60 frames per second, such as a streamer's capture-card and upscaling setup, or waiting for a version that runs at 60.
Spam built around the Dancer emote, telling chat to dance or to "dance away" a problem, often in chains alternating the emote with words.
Chanted in chat as part of mock socialist slogans like "honor and dignity" and "dignity for all".
The Star Wars TV show, which chat debated (overrated or great, how political it is) and was surprised Destiny hadn't seen.
Short for Sam Altman, whom chat jokingly blames for buying up RAM and pushing up its price, and whose looks chat mocks.
Chat's term for the streamer awards broadcast it watched, used for commentary on the hosts, guests, outfits and sponsors.
Mostly part of "Chris Hansen". Chat brings him up in connection with the movie Primetime, asking what he thinks of it and comparing him to characters in it.
Almost always part of 'race realism', chat's label for the stream segment debating race realist arguments.
